title: Days at or above 95°F
unit: days a year with a county-average high of 95°F or more
release: NOAA NCEI nClimGrid-Daily v1.0.0, scaled county averages
geographyVintage: NOAA county area averages; joined by FIPS through NOAA's state-code crosswalk
note: This value is the mean number of days a year from 1991–2020. On those days, the county's area-average daily high reached 95°F. NOAA estimates values between weather stations on a 5 km grid. It then averages the grid over the county. So this is a smoothed climate normal, not a thermometer reading. It hides urban heat islands and elevation differences within a county. The same 95°F means different things in humid and dry places. It is not a projection of future heat. Source: NOAA NCEI nClimGrid-Daily v1.0.0. NOAA does not endorse this atlas.

51678.reason: NOAA publishes no separate area average for Lexington city. Rockbridge County surrounds the city. No value is borrowed from the surrounding county.
